title: The Preamble and Features of the Indian Constitution

facts.text: On 13th December 1946, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru presented the 'Objectives Resolution' before the Constituent Assembly.
facts.quote: On 13th December 1946, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru presented the 'Objectives Resolution' before the Constituent Assembly

facts.text: The Preamble (or Preface) to the Indian Constitution evolved from the Objectives Resolution.
facts.quote: subsequently, the Preamble (or Preface) to the Indian Constitution evolved from this very resolution.

facts.text: The Preamble is also called the 'Introduction', 'Objectives' or 'Preface'.
facts.quote: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution is also referred to as the 'Introduction', 'Objectives', or 'Preface'.

facts.text: The Preamble explains the values and objectives of the Constitution, so it is often described as the 'Soul' of the Constitution.
facts.quote: The Preamble to the Constitution elucidates the values and objectives of the Constitution. Therefore, the Preamble is often described as the 'Soul' of the Constitution.

facts.text: The Constitution of India has been framed by the people of India and voluntarily adopted by them.
facts.quote: The Constitution of India has been framed by the people of India and has been voluntarily adopted by them.

facts.text: The Preamble declares India to be a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic'.
facts.quote: In the Preamble to the Constitution, India is declared to be a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.'

facts.text: Sovereign: a country over which no external power has control and which is completely independent to make its own decisions.
facts.quote: Sovereign : A country over which no external power exercises control and which is completely independent to make its own decisions, is termed a 'Sovereign' nation.

facts.text: India has the supreme authority to enact its own laws and to formulate its foreign policy.
facts.quote: India possesses the supreme authority to enact its own laws and to formulate its foreign policy.

facts.text: Socialist: the nation's wealth is generated collectively by society and the State (government) holds ownership over it.
facts.quote: Socialist : The wealth of the nation is generated collectively by society and the State (government) holds ownership over it. This is known as a 'Socialist' system.

facts.text: The aim of the socialist system is to reduce economic and social inequalities, so that wealth does not become concentrated in a few hands.
facts.quote: Its objective is to reduce economic and social inequalities within society, ensuring that wealth does not become concentrated in a few hands.

facts.text: Secular: the State has no official religion of its own; all religions are treated with equal respect and every citizen is free to practise their religion.
facts.quote: Secular : 'Secular' implies that the State (the country) does not have any official religion of its own. All religions are treated with equal respect and every citizen enjoys complete freedom to practice their religion in accordance with their own faith.

facts.text: Democratic: the people are the ultimate source of power and elect their own representatives.
facts.quote: Democratic : 'Democratic' implies that the people constitute the ultimate source of power and they themselves elect their own representatives.

facts.text: Democracy is identified as 'government of the people, by the people and for the people'.
facts.quote: This system is identified as 'government of the people, by the people and for the people.'

facts.text: Republic: no public office in the country (such as President, Prime Minister, Chief Minister, Mayor, Sarpanch) is held on a hereditary basis.
facts.quote: Republic : A republic implies that no public office in the country (for instance: President, Prime Minister, Chief Minister, Mayor, Sarpanch etc.) is held on a hereditary basis.

facts.text: In a republic, offices are held by representatives elected by the people, directly or indirectly, for a specific tenure.
facts.quote: Instead, these offices are held by representatives elected by the people either directly or indirectly for a specific tenure.

facts.text: The Constitution aims to build India on the values of Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity, which emerged from India's struggle for independence.
facts.quote: The Constitution has adopted the objective of establishing India based on the values of Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity values that emerged from India's struggle for independence.

facts.text: Justice means equal opportunities for progress to everyone without discrimination based on caste, religion, race, gender or language.
facts.quote: Justice : Justice means providing equal opportunities for progress to everyone, without subjecting anyone to discrimination based on caste, religion, race, gender or language.

facts.text: Justice includes social, economic and political justice.
facts.quote: This includes social, economic and political justice.

facts.text: Liberty means no unreasonable restrictions on citizens and an environment that helps the development of their personalities.
facts.quote: Liberty : Liberty implies the absence of any unreasonable restrictions on citizens and the existence of an environment conducive to the development of their personalities.

facts.text: Liberty includes freedom of thought, expression, movement, association, occupation, faith and worship.
facts.quote: This includes freedom of thought, expression, movement, association, occupation, faith and worship.

facts.text: Equality means equal status to everyone, with no one treated as superior or inferior because of caste, religion, race, gender, language or place of birth.
facts.quote: Equality : Equality means granting equal status to everyone, without treating anyone as superior or inferior based on caste, religion, race, gender, language or place of birth.

facts.text: Fraternity is a sense of unity and belonging among all citizens; it upholds the dignity of the individual and strengthens the unity of the nation.
facts.quote: Fraternity : Fraternity signifies the existence of a sense of unity and belonging among all citizens of the country. This sentiment upholds the dignity of the individual and strengthens the unity of the nation.

facts.text: Among all the written constitutions in the world, the Constitution of India is the largest.
facts.quote: India's Constitution is extremely comprehensive, profound and extensive. Among all the written constitutions in the world, the Constitution of India is the largest.

facts.text: After studying constitutions across the globe, the Constituent Assembly included in India's Constitution the elements most suitable for the country.
facts.quote: After studying various constitutions across the globe, the Constituent Assembly incorporated into India's Constitution those elements deemed most suitable for the country.

facts.text: A flexible constitution can be easily amended; a rigid constitution is extremely difficult to amend; India's Constitution is a blend of both.
facts.quote: A constitution in which provisions can be easily amended is termed a 'flexible constitution.' Conversely, a constitution in which amending provisions is extremely difficult is termed a 'rigid constitution.' The Constitution of India represents a blend of both rigidity and flexibility.

facts.text: The Constitution grants fundamental rights to all citizens of India and has entrusted the Judiciary with safeguarding them.
facts.quote: Indian Constitution has granted fundamental rights to all citizens of India. The responsibility for safeguarding these rights has been entrusted with the Judiciary by the Constitution.

facts.text: Along with fundamental rights, the Constitution prescribes fundamental duties, which every Indian citizen is expected to follow.
facts.quote: Along with fundamental rights, the Indian Constitution has also prescribed certain fundamental duties. Every Indian citizen is expected to abide by these fundamental duties.

facts.text: The Constitution outlines Directive Principles of State Policy; governance is expected to follow these guiding principles.
facts.quote: The Indian Constitution outlines a set of Directive Principles. The governance is expected to be conducted in accordance with these guiding principles.

facts.text: Federal system: India is a Union of States; the Constitution divides powers between the Union (Central) Government and the State Governments.
facts.quote: India is a Union of States. The Constitution has demarcated the powers between the Union (Central) Government and the State Governments.

facts.text: Parliament makes laws on subjects at the central level; the State Legislature makes laws on subjects at the state level.
facts.quote: While the Parliament is empowered to enact laws regarding subjects at the central level, the State Legislature is empowered to enact laws regarding subjects at the state level.

facts.text: In a parliamentary democracy, voters elect representatives; the Prime Minister is elected from among them and selects his/her Council of Ministers.
facts.quote: In a parliamentary democracy, voters elect their representatives. From among these elected representatives, country's Prime Minister gets elected and the Prime Minister, in turn, selects his/her Council of Ministers.

facts.text: Universal Adult Franchise: any Indian citizen who has reached the age of 18 years has the right to vote.
facts.quote: Any Indian citizen who has attained the age of 18 years possesses the right to vote; this is known as Universal Adult Franchise.

facts.text: Prominent members from Maharashtra in the Constituent Assembly: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh, Shri Keshavrao Jedhe, Dr. Durgabai Deshmukh, Shri Shankarrao Dev, Shri Narhar Gadgil, Shri Balasaheb Khardekar, Shri Dada Dharmadhikari, Shri Brajlal Biyani and Shri Madhav (Bapuji) Aney.
facts.quote: Some Prominent Members from Maharashtra in the Constituent Assembly Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Shri Keshavrao Jedhe Dr. Durgabai Deshmukh Shri Shankarrao Dev Shri Narhar Gadgil Shri Balasaheb Khardekar Shri Dada Dharmadhikari Shri Brajlal Biyani Shri Madhav (Bapuji) Aney

facts.text: The Constitution has placed 'Rights' in one pan of the scale and 'Duties' in the other.
facts.quote: Concept : The Constitution has placed 'Rights' in one pan of the scale and 'Duties' in the other.
